obligations.note: The change adds a category rule to purge_due so closed tax_authority payees are never purged, even though they hold NPI (account_number, routing_number, tax_id, date_of_birth per the store schema). RET-1 allows only legal hold as a reason to keep NPI past the retention period; the sampled control test only uses vendor payees and never exercises this case.
This deviation from RET-1 is not covered by any exception: the register has no entry for RET-1 or for payments.retention (it only has SES-1, LOG-1 and a withdrawn MFA-1 entry).

Ticket CHG-25557 is a standard ticket, approved on 2026-10-22 by erik.brandt (change_manager) before the review. Its component payments.retention covers the only touched file, apps/baseline-payments/payments/retention.py.
The code_review approval comes from sofia.santos, a change_approver for payments and a different person from the author jonah.weiss (p-jweiss).
The approval names head commit bfa403d, which is the only commit in the change.

records/ci/run.json shows pr-checks succeeded on bfa403d. The JUnit report has 172 tests, 0 failures and 0 skipped, including the RET-1 control test test_sampled_purge_respects_hold (sample coverage). However, the report's timestamp and hostname do not match the run record, and I could not re-run the suite locally (pytest not installed).
No acceptance-ledger entry covers retention.py, so the change does not invalidate any earlier evidence.

summary: PR-1209 adds a rule to payments' retention job that permanently skips purging NPI of closed tax_authority payees. RET-1 requires closed payees' NPI to be purged after the approved retention period, with legal hold as the only exception, and tax-authority payees hold the same NPI fields as other payees. There is no approved exception for RET-1 on payments.retention, and the sampled control test passes only because it never creates a tax-authority payee. The process obligations (ticket, independent approval of the final commit, CI) are met, but the product violation requires rejection.
